effect: An adopted UN Security Council sanctions resolution (asset freeze and arms embargo) now binds every UN member except the target, as Chapter VII decisions bind all UN members (UN Charter Art. 25, 41, 48), instead of only the Council members that voted yes. Membership is the game's own test (kF: a sovereign or micro state in the game's status table, the same test as the UN screen), so observer and partly recognised states (Palestine, Taiwan) stay out. Each country still receives only the instruments it can apply (YK/F1e: the asset freeze needs a reserve-currency issuer, so most members join with the arms embargo alone), and its enforcement is still chosen by the game from its alignment with the target (lax 35 % leak for friends, standard 10 %, strict 2 %), so the target's partners comply loosely, as in reality. The resolution's sponsor is recorded as the regime's initiator (the game otherwise takes the first participant; the initiator is never lax). The player's country joins only if the player voted yes, as the vote screen promises ('A yes from you would commit you too'); the player can still join by hand. Release: the game ends a UN regime only when a nuclear-acquisition target disarms (Zg/gL); for a resolution on an aggression dossier, the countries this patch enrolled (participants who did not vote yes) now leave the regime once the war named in the dossier has ended (checked whenever the game reviews sanctions, Zg: at a war's end and in the monthly review), and the regime ends if nobody is left. The yes voters stay, as in the game. Resolutions on annexation, war crimes, crimes against humanity or nuclear use keep everyone, as the game keeps its yes voters; real UN sanctions end only when the Council lifts them. Side effect: each enrolled country records a mild sanction grudge in the target's memory (bp(...,'sanction'), relation hit 0), as the yes voters already do. No new state (the enrolled set is read from the resolution's saved votes). No day-0 effect (no resolution is adopted at day 0). Single player: the player exception reads the session's player country.
